entities.summary: Francis Stebbins Bartow was an American lawyer and politician from Georgia. He served two terms in the United States House of Representatives and became a politician in the Confederate States of America. Bartow was also a colonel in the Georgia Militia commanding the 21st Oglethorpe Light Infantry during the early months of the American Civil War. Bartow was a delegate from Georgia's 1st congressional district to the Southern Convention in Montgomery, Alabama becoming an inaugurating member of the Confederate Provisional Congress—leading efforts to prepare local forces in the aftermath of secession, protracting into The American Civil War of 1861–65.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a delegate from Georgia's 1st congressional district to the Southern Convention and an inaugural member of the Confederate Provisional Congress, Bartow played a key role in preparing local forces for secession, contributing to the outbreak of the American Civil War. His involvement had significant regional impact on the conflict.
